summary: HTTP monitoring, public status-page configuration, incident timelines, and scheduled maintenance with exact assertions, component mappings, and response-time visibility.

capabilities.notes: Preserve the complete request, cadence, regions, active state, redirects, retries, timeout, and assertion semantics.
Map source groups and cards to destination monitor IDs; do not infer a component relationship from similar names.
Public monitor visibility and public response-time views require separate verification after enough check intervals.
Map Hyperping public incidents to OpenStatus status reports, not automatic monitor incidents. Preserve the earliest real timeline timestamp and component scope.
Replay updates chronologically with notifications disabled. Hyperping update entries without a phase carry the latest known target phase.
Preserve title, schedule, component scope, and message. The target derives maintenance state from its schedule and has no separate maintenance-update timeline.
Archive source monitor check history separately; no warranted historical-check import path exists.
Reauthorize and test provider-specific notification endpoints instead of copying credentials or silently changing routing.
